language.title: Language
language.blurb: The language the Studio speaks. English is the source; a language that misses a line shows it in English. The game's own messages (errors, warnings, the Monitor's log lines) stay as the game writes them.
language.contribute: Another language is one file: src/locales/<code>.json in the Studio's repository, proposed like anything else there.

settings.title: Settings
settings.blurb: Where your game and mods live, which warnings you see, and what the Build 42 shim covers.
settings.notFoundHere: The Studio cannot find the game here
settings.gameDirBlurb: Root installation folder containing ProjectZomboid64.exe and base game files. Compatible with Steam, GOG or manual installations.
settings.workshopDir: Steam Workshop Folder (Optional if not using Steam)
settings.workshopDirBlurb: For Steam users: Path where Workshop mods are downloaded (workshop/content/108600). If you play on GOG or install mods manually in Zomboid/mods, you can leave this field empty.
settings.userDir: User Zomboid Directory (Data and Local Mods Folder)
settings.userDirBlurb: User personal folder (C:\Users\<User>\Zomboid). Contains logs (console.txt), saves, profiles and the local mods folder (Zomboid/mods).
settings.modListBlurb: The file the game reads to know which mods are on and in what order. Found automatically at Zomboid/mods/default.txt.
settings.chooseWarnings: Choose which warnings the Studio shows you.
settings.noMergeWarning: Warning when launching game without active merge package
settings.noMergeWarningBlurb: Warn me before launching when no merge package is active to resolve collisions between mods.
settings.sortNoticeBlurb: Shows an explanatory informational dialog when clicking the sort dependencies button in the mod list.
settings.startupQuestion: What should open when the Studio starts?
settings.profilesStartBlurb: Shows the profile manager so you can choose or activate the combination you are going to work with.
settings.openLastBlurb: Loads the previous active profile and takes you directly to the mod list.
settings.rememberModeBlurb: The Launch button starts on the mode you used last time (Debug, Windowed, Normal...). Off: it always starts on Debug Mode (Fullscreen), the recommended one.
settings.community: Download the community rules and mod index
settings.communityBlurb: Once a day, from the Studio's own repository on GitHub: load-order rules, incompatible pairs, and one registry per mod with the builds it runs on, what it clashes with and its known issues with the fix the Studio can apply. Auto-Sort, Mod Health, the Mod List and the Browse page use them. Off: the last copy is kept and nothing is fetched. Nothing is ever sent.
settings.github: GitHub token, for "Propose" in one click
settings.githubBlurb: Optional. With a personal token saved, "Propose to the community" (a load-order rule, a mod's registry) forks the Studio's repository on your account once, writes the file on a branch and opens the pull request by itself. Without one, the same buttons open GitHub's page with the JSON filled in and you press "Propose changes" there. Receiving the community files needs no account at all. The token is checked with GitHub and kept in Windows Credential Manager on this PC only; nothing else is ever sent.
settings.githubHow: Make a fine-grained token on GitHub (Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens) for your own repositories with "Contents" and "Pull requests" read and write; it is used only on your fork and to open the pull request.
settings.removeTokenConfirm: Remove the saved GitHub token from this PC?
settings.developerBlurb: Shows the Developer screen, the MCP agent server, which lets an AI assistant drive the Studio, and the companion mod that runs commands inside the game. Nothing a player needs; leave it off unless you are building with it.
settings.shimBlurb: Many Build 41 mods call things Build 42 renamed or removed, and crash. The Studio ships one shim that patches those calls at runtime, and writes it into every merge package you build. Parts 1 to 6 are all or nothing: they guard the game's own code and need nothing from you beyond a merge package being active. Part 7 patches particular mods, and each of those has a switch below.
settings.shimUnreadable: The shim could not be read from this build of the Studio.
settings.perModNote: each runs only while its mod is active; off = the shim leaves that mod alone
settings.patchOnTitle: On: the shim patches this mod while it is active. Click to switch it off.
settings.patchOffTitle: Off: the shim leaves this mod alone. Click to switch it on.
settings.patchWritten: {{label}} is {{state}}. Written into {{count}} package(s); the game reads it on its next launch.
settings.switchNote: A switch is written into every Studio package on disk at once, as Z_PZModStudio_Patches.lua; no publish needed, the game reads it when it next starts.

mcp.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server
mcp.blurb: Connect autonomous AI agents (Antigravity, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code with Roo Code/Cline, or local models via Ollama/LM Studio) directly to PZ Mod Studio. The MCP server gives them the console log, crash reports, the files two mods both replace, a Lua syntax check and control of the running game.
mcp.generatorBlurb: Select your AI client or environment and copy the JSON snippet into your configuration file:
mcp.important: Important: Do NOT run pz-mcp-server.exe directly by double-clicking
mcp.importantBlurb: If you double-click pz-mcp-server.exe, a black command prompt will open and stay blank. This is completely normal. The MCP server communicates silently over stdio (JSON-RPC) with AI agents. You do not need to keep it open; your AI assistant (Claude, Cursor, Antigravity) will launch and close it automatically in the background whenever you send prompts in chat.

row.loadTimeTitle:
Loading time: of the time the game spent on the loading screen last session, {{time}} went to reading this mod's files.

Most mods take a few milliseconds; tile and model packs take seconds. It says nothing about how the mod runs once loaded.

Measured from the game's own DebugLog (Zomboid/Logs), from this mod's "loading" line to the next mod's; the Lua phase after that is one pass and is not timed per mod.

row.warningsTitle: Last session the game logged {{count}} warning(s) about this mod: the game noticed something odd and carried on, so nothing broke by itself.
row.requireNote: (require(...) failed: the mod asked for a file the game could not find at that path. Harmless unless a feature is missing; the Monitor Center can fix the path.)
row.fromConsole: From console.txt as it is now; the Monitor Center has the full cards.
